packet.claim: recover_json_object skips fenced JSON objects with duplicate keys instead of resolving them last-wins, so a later top-level object can be scored even though a fenced object exists.
packet.expected: The last fenced object with duplicate keys should be parsed with last-wins and returned, because the rules say any candidate that parses as strict JSON or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins is scoreable, and the last fenced object is preferred when any fence holds one.
packet.observed: The fenced pool only attempts loads_strict; on duplicate keys it sets parsed=None and continues. The top-level pool then scans all objects, including the fenced one, but reversed order may pick a later top-level object outside the fence, returning that instead.
packet.scope: Replies containing a fenced JSON object with duplicate keys followed by a later top-level JSON object outside any fence.
packet.source_basis: Docstring: 'A candidate that parses as strict JSON, or as JSON with repeated keys resolved last-wins, is scoreable' and 'The object scored is the last one inside a code fence when any fence holds one'. Source comment: 'A reply that is otherwise one well-formed object with a repeated key is still scoreable: take the last value for each key'.
packet.uncertainty: Assumes loads_strict rejects duplicate keys as documented; not executed.
